title: Evacuation and go-bag
summary: When to leave, what to pack, and what to do before you lock the door. The T1D go-kit has its own guide.

blocks.text: **When to leave:** when local officials tell you to. Leave early enough to beat severe weather. If you live in a mandatory evacuation zone and officials order it, **leave immediately**. Be ready to go on foot if the disaster requires it.
Virginia's Know Your Zone program covers 23 coastal localities, **not Henrico**. Henrico will use its own alerts and officials' instructions. Sign up for Henrico County Alert and the FEMA app.

items: Pick several destinations in different directions (a friend's home in another town, a motel).
Learn alternate routes and other ways out of your area.
Make a household communication plan: a meeting place and an **out-of-state contact**.
Pets: choose a place that accepts pets. Most public shelters take only service animals.
Shelters change from event to event. Ask Henrico Emergency Management at (804) 501-5162, dial 2-1-1, or use the FEMA app.
**Keep at least half a tank of gas** in the car at all times. Fill up when evacuation looks likely. Take one car per family.
Water (1 gallon per person per day) and non-perishable food
Battery-powered or hand-crank radio, NOAA Weather Radio with tone alert
Flashlight and extra batteries
Phone chargers and a backup battery
First-aid kit
Prescription medicines with prescriptions, plus over-the-counter medicines
Glasses or contact lenses and solution
Whistle to signal for help
Dust mask
Plastic sheeting, scissors and duct tape (to shelter in place)
Moist towelettes, garbage bags and plastic ties for sanitation
Hygiene items
Wrench or pliers to turn off utilities
Manual can opener
Local maps
Pet food and extra water for pets
Copies of insurance policies and IDs (also saved in a password-protected digital space)

blocks.text: **Type 1 diabetes:** see the T1D go-kit guide for insulin, glucose, glucagon, pump and sensor supplies. Pack it with your go-bag.

items: Lock up the home and unplug small electrical equipment.
Keep refrigerators and freezers plugged in unless flooding is a risk.
Leave a note saying where you went.
Follow recommended routes. Avoid shortcuts. Stay away from flooded areas, washed-out roads and downed power lines.
**Don't drive through flood water.** 6 inches of fast water can knock you down. 1 foot can sweep a car away.

blocks.text: If Virginia orders an evacuation for a nuclear plant, plan to be away from home **at least 3 days** and go to the nearest Evacuation Assembly Center. See the nuclear guide.

items: Check with officials before returning. Don't go back until debris is cleared.
Bring water and non-perishable food for the trip home and fill the gas tank before you leave.
Generators run **outdoors only**, away from the house.

blocks.text: Blankets, water, snacks, warm coat and boots, first-aid kit, flashlight, hand warmers, ice scraper, shovel, sand or cat litter for traction, jumper cables, road flares, cash, paper map, phone power bank, extra medicine, garbage bags.
